title.narrative: EU-Kiribati Partnership : Building resilience through improved sanitation (BRIS) - UNICEF

description.narrative: This Action is part of the larger programme: EU-Kiribati Partnership for a sustainable and inclusive socio-economic development. The overall objective is to support Kiribati in building greater socio-economic and climate resilience. The Specific objective is to improve the use of services and goods provided by the public sector with a focus on water and sanitation in the Line Islands. This CA covers 2 out of 4 components of the broader Partnership:Component 3 - Improved access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene Component 4 - Strengthened community, household and institutional resilience for water, sanitation and hygiene.

comment.narrative: Two Healthcare facilities benefitted from minor maintenance works on existing structures following the 2022 world toilet day rapid assessment. In the reporting year working with MLPID and its Civil Division WASH infrastructure assessments were completed in all 9 healthcare facilities in the three Line Islands. A bill of quantities for construction material was completed in February 2023 and a tender for the works was developed with work to be initiated in the next reporting period. Three round of bidding was launched with two round resulting without any bid and the third round with overtly expensive bid. Modality is adapted now to procure supplies and undertake construction by construction water and sanitation department.

title.narrative: of households provided with rebates or subsidies for compliance with WASH best practices

description.narrative: of households provided with rebates or subsidies for compliance with WASH best practices

comment.narrative: The Rebate Compliance Framework has been finalized and translated into the Kiribati language. A multisectoral team assessed 96 households based on compliance criteria awarding rebates to 89 of them. Among these 46 households HH received the full rebate of 500 AUD while the remaining households received partial rebates ranging from 200 AUD to 350 AUD. Based on the request from the government implementation approach is changed from rebate to subsidy. Full subsidies in supplies approximately AUD 1000 per HH to construct lined septic concrete ring toilet slab water closet plumbing supplies and supplies for roofing materials will be provided to over 360 HH on Kiritimati Island. Around 240 HH on Kiritimati will be provided with partial subsidy to construct septic ring and toilet slab.Subsidy for outer islands Teraina and Tabuaeran will be finalized following the community mobilization and consultation.

comment.narrative: All 12 schools and 9 healthcare facilities in the Line Islands

The 3star approach was introduced to all target schools and healthcare facilities. During this reporting period all staff and members of the management committees at two schools Gulfport primary and SPIVE secondary school were trained in WASH in schools with a particular focus on the 3star approach. Training for the remaining schools and healthcare facilities is scheduled to continue next year.

title.narrative: of people informed about good sanitation practices

description.narrative: of people informed about good sanitation practices

comment.narrative: In partnership with KILGA radio messages in the form of dialogues were developed in both English and Kiribati. These are aimed at raising awareness on the project objectives and helping people understand the meaning of acronyms related to WASH with each component being explained and their significance to human health. The listenership of the radio messages could not be ascertained but it is assumed that the broadcast reaches all three target islands.Working with the island councils the team is developing communication material about WASH standards at household levels to raise awareness among households and to promote advocacy through elected officials. Through Data analysis the project has noted the need to focus messaging to preschool pupils and caregivers of under five children. The project will adopt the baby WASH programming approach which provides guidance on how to engage toddlers and their care givers especially around hygiene behaviour change.

title.narrative: Status of sanitation objectives within MLPID development strategy in Line Islands

description.narrative: Status of sanitation objectives within MLPID development strategy in Line Islands

comment.narrative: Sanitation objectives yet to be fully defined and addressed
MLPID sanitation objectives fully defined and addressed

WASH financing study gave financial projections to MLPID towards meeting their 100 per cent sanitation targets. The ongoing development of the faecal management plan will form the basis to achieve MLPIDs sanitation objectives. Both reports will guide the ministry in deciding whether to continue with rebates and subsidies beyond the current project support.The MIPLD sanitation objective is clearly defined to attain ODF islands. The FSM is now finalized and ready to be piloted to reach upper level of sanitation service ladder. The findings from this pilot will guide the way forward to reach safely managed sanitation services. Environmental License for Faecal Sludge Management has been submitted to MELAD.

title.narrative: Status of National WASH sector plans integrating climate resilient development and/or risk management strategies

description.narrative: Status of National WASH sector plans integrating climate resilient development and/or risk management strategies

comment.narrative: Sustainable WASH plans developed though not implemented
Sustainable WASH plans developed and implemented in the Line Islands

In line with the Kiribati Joint Implementation Plan for Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management KJIP 20142023 UNICEF is supporting Office of the President the Kiribati National Experts Group as well the Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy MISE the WASH sector led to conduct a WASH climate change literature review for Kiribati as well as develop a WASH Climate rational for the country. The outcomes will guide the key SDG indicators to be integrated into national WASH sector plans. At the Line Island level in partnership with KILGA all target Islands through their councils have develop WASH policies and actions plans to guide WASH developments. These plans are of more significance to the two outer islands of Tabuaeran and Teraina where the council has full responsibility for WASH development. On Kiritimati Islands MLPID has begun working with the Urban Council to implement the WASH Action plan. Due to the constraints noted in D08.1 the integration of Climate change and Disaster Risk reduction in island council development strategies will be completed in the next reporting period. However the first session with Kiritimati urban council and stakeholders is planned for 2nd June 2023

title.narrative: % of new and existing dwellings compliant with new sanitation and hygiene regulations

description.narrative: % of new and existing dwellings compliant with new sanitation and hygiene regulations

comment.narrative: 50 existing dwellings and 80 new dwellings compliant with new regulations

In line with R2.1.7 UNICEF will be supporting the Lands Board and MLPID to develop a monitoring and compliance framework based on already existing assessments and criteria. A recent compliance assessment by the Land Board of 61 HH in Main Camp Village showed that 10 HH were in compliance while 29 were noncompliant to toilet design submitted and 22 did not have a toilet. The project will be supporting the Land Board to complete the assessment across Kiritimati the outcome will indicate the compliance or lack of compliance to sanitation among lease holders. The assessment will lead to the identification of lease holders who would qualify for the rebate program if endorsed by MLPID. In addition it would give feedback on the reasons for noncompliance and no construction among lease holders.

comment.narrative: 12 schools 9 healthcare facilities and 20 communities ward councils with sustainable WASH plans developed and implemented

The two schools that received training have established baseline for 2024 and developed school WASH improvement plans. The remaining schools will undertake similar preparations following their training. The training for the other schools is scheduled to be completed by end of this year. Additionally the newly formed Ward WASH Committees will receive training on sustainability enabling them to prepare WASH safety and security plans.

comment.narrative: WASH safety plans drafted endorsed embedded and actioned within all 3 island council strategic plans

At the line Island level in partnership with KILGA all target Islands through their councils have developed WASH policies and action plans to guide WASH developments. For Kiritimati Islands MLPID is working with urban council to implement the WASH action plan.In August 2023 KILGA facilitated the preparation of the risk profiles for Tabuaeran and Teraina Islands. This endeavour involved contributions from communitybased organizations CBOs working on disaster risk reduction DRR alongside the full councils. The primary focus of the discussions includeda Risks to the island populationb Risks to WASH infrastructure and systemsc Mechanisms for dealing with natural disasters.WASH safety and security plan is being reviewedupdated.
